GOAL: pick a coupling position not used by the rejected arms (OCCURV-FIELD per-occupant curvature on residual, strataot-curv stratified curvature + behaviour-marginal Sinkhorn, brancurv-l1 branching-adaptive radial level-1, plus cross-graph dual-segment transport, capacity units, per-code curvature field, hierarchical curvature + Sinkhorn).
READ: task text only; workspace contains a single empty progress.jsonl, so the repo/contract file is not readable here; all geometry conventions are therefore taken verbatim from the contract summary quoted in the task (ball curvature kappa=-c, R_c=1/sqrt(c), d_c=(2/sqrt c) artanh(sqrt c ||(-x)(+)y||), exp_0^c(v)=tanh(sqrt c ||v||) v/(sqrt c ||v||)).
OBSERVED: none of the rejected arms uses (i) a per-codeword, demand-derived ADDITIVE BIAS on the level-1 distance, nor (ii) a curved-distance SOFT ASSIGNMENT that feeds the behaviour statistic itself (closing a geometry->behaviour->geometry loop). Both are cheap, only touch level 1, and keep the baseline loss/STE untouched.

The idea chosen is L1PDO-RQ: level-1 Poincare distance minus a mean-centred log-demand offset, where the demand statistic is measured through the same curved softmax assignment. Removing either switch changes the same argmin, so the coupling is real and single-run testable.

TITLE: Level-1 Poincare demand offset: a curved level-1 distance biased by a curvature-measured codeword demand, leaving levels 2-3 and the loss exactly as baseline.

NOVELTY: Unlike the rejected arms there is no per-code curvature field, no stratified/marginal Sinkhorn, no radial branching coordinate, no capacity unit and no second transport segment. Levels 2 and 3, the reconstruction loss, the commitment term and the straight-through estimator are byte-identical to baseline.

exp_0^c(v) = tanh(sqrt c ||v||) * v / (sqrt c ||v||), exp_0^c(0) = 0;
(-x)(+)y is Moebius addition:
 x (+) y = ((1 + 2c<x,y> + c^2||y||^2) x + (1 - c||x||^2) y) / (1 + 2c<x,y> + c^2||x||^2||y||^2).
Frozen measured constants (no tuning):
 s = sqrt( mean_i ||r1_i||^2 ) over the level-1 encoder latents, running mean over the first 50 optimiser steps, then frozen as a buffer.
 c = 1 in the frame v = r1 / s (documented default: ball radius = data RMS tangent radius, so bulk radius tanh(1) = 0.762 and saturation is bounded at 0.964 for a 2 sigma item).
 tau = running mean over the same 50 steps of mean_i min_k d_c(u_i, q_k), clamped to [0.01, 10], frozen (measured local distance scale, used only as the softmax temperature).
 w = beta, the baseline commitment weight, documented default 0.25.
 rho = 1/48 (EMA horizon = two epochs = 48 steps).
Batched computation, every step, level 1 only:
 v_i = r1_i / s ;  u_i = exp_0^c(v_i) ;  q_k = exp_0^c(a^(1)_k)   (a^(1) = baseline level-1 codebook, unchanged parameter)
 S_ik = softmax_k( -d_c(u_i, q_k) / tau )                       (detached scalars, no grad)
 m_k = sum_i S_ik * D_i ,  n_k = sum_i S_ik ,  raw_k = m_k / max(n_k, 1e-8)
 demand_k <- (1-rho) demand_k + rho * raw_k * K1 / max(sum_j raw_j, 1e-8)   (init demand_k = 1; for steps < 50 demand_k = 1)
 ell_k = log1p(demand_k) ; off_k = beta * clip(ell_k - mean_j ell_j, -ln 3, +ln 3)   (detached)

k1(i) = argmin_k ( d_c(u_i, q_k) - off_k ), ties -> smallest k

D_i (item transition demand) is precomputed once from the TRAINING split only: D_i = number of times item i occurs as the next item over all consecutive pairs of the training sequences, then divided by its mean over training items (so mean_i D_i = 1) and stored float32, requires_grad = False.
Gradient rules: forward uses the hard k1; no new differentiable term is added; off_k, S_ik, demand_k, s, tau, c, D_i are all detached/frozen. The parameter update changes only because a different codeword is selected (different a^(1)_{k1} in r2 and in the reconstruction of levels 2-3, hence different reconstruction and commitment gradients on the level-1 codebook rows and on the encoder). Argmin is non-differentiable; STE is left exactly as baseline.
Training integration: no extra epoch, no extra loss, no schedule change; only level-1 forward assignment differs.
Switches (present in code, no arm trained): BEHAVIOUR_OFF=true sets D_i = 1 for all i => raw_k = 1 => demand_k = 1 => ell_k - mean = 0 => off_k = 0 (pure curved assignment). GEOMETRY_OFF=true sets c = 0, which in the same formulas gives exp_0 = identity, d_c = 2||x - y||, so k1 = argmin_k (2||v_i - a_k|| - off_k) (Euclidean, the 2x factor is argmin-invariant). Both switches read at module init and logged in the run config.
COST: 72,000 optimiser steps in total (24 steps/epoch x 3000 epochs) at 24,556 training items, unchanged from baseline. Per step the only additions are, with batch B = 1024, K1 = 256 level-1 codes and latent dim 64: one [1024,256,64] Moebius-add + norm + artanh block (~17M elements, roughly 10 flops each = ~0.17 GFLOP, a few elementwise kernels) plus one [1024,256] softmax and one [256] EMA update; that is well under 2% of a transformer step, so expect <= +3% wall clock over the full 3000 epochs and no extra memory beyond a [B,K1] matrix. HYPOTHESIS: If first-token partitioning is limited by the absence of behavioural structure rather than by reconstruction geometry, then biasing the level-1 curved assignment with a curvature-measured transition demand should raise Stage3 test recall@10 above the 0.0555 baseline toward / past 0.065 in a single run, and it must show up as (a) a level-1 code-usage distribution whose per-code offset correlates with per-code assignment share and (b) an improved first-token hit rate for the held-out next item when predicted from the history's SID prefixes, with the reconstruction loss not degrading materially.

- demand EMA can be hijacked by a few very popular codewords, producing a self-reinforcing rich-get-richer loop (offset raises assignment share, which raises demand).
- at data RMS radius 0.762 the Poincare metric is only mildly different from Euclidean, so the geometry switch may be a near no-op and the effect would come from the offset alone.
- the change is discrete (argmin) and may barely alter the optimisation path, so the single run

could be indistinguishable from baseline within seed noise.
- D_i from raw transition counts is popularity-heavy; centring and the ln 3 clip may be too weak to expose co-consumption structure.
- first-level reassignment could make levels 2-3 absorb residual mass that they were not sized for, leaving SID collisions/shorteffective prefixes.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Training-only directed item-transition demand: the mean-normalised in-degree D_i of each training item (how often it is the next item in the training sequences), aggregated into per-first-level-codeword demand through the model's own curved soft assignment and EMA-smoothed.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the training split interaction sequences only: for every consecutive pair (u_t -> u_{t+1}) in each training sequence, increment count[u_{t+1}]; then D_i = count[i] / mean_j count[j] over the 24,556 training items (items never appearing as a next item get D_i = 0 and are floored at exp(-3) through the clip on ell_k). LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: D_i uses only training-split transitions; no validation or test interaction, no test user, no test item and no Stage3 label enters D_i, s, tau, c or off_k. s and tau are measured from training latents only during the first 50 training steps, before any evaluation. off_k is one scalar per code - it never stores per-item or per-user information, so no validation/test item identity can be memorised into the SID construction, and the SID vocabulary is produced by the same encoder/codebook for all splits with no split-dependent state. Levels 2-3, the loss and the STE are untouched.

COUPLING EQUATION: k1(i) = argmin_k [ d_c( exp_0^c(r1_i / s), exp_0^c(a^(1)_k) ) - beta * clip( log1p(demand_k) - mean_j log1p(demand_j), -ln 3, +ln 3 ) ] with demand_k = EMA_rho( sum_i S_ik D_i / sum_i S_ik ), S_ik = softmax_k( -d_c(u_i, q_k) / tau ); the behaviour term is D_i / demand_k, the curved term is d_c(exp_0^c(.), exp_0^c(.)) and both meet inside the single argmin.

assignment (forward-only diagnostic, logged, not used to select anything); (2) level-1 code usage entropy and the correlation between per-code off_k and per-code assignment share (the loop should be visible as positive correlation, capped by the ln 3 clip); (3) first-token predictability: hit rate of the true next item's level-1 token given the history's SID prefix, recorded as a diagnostic; (4) reconstruction loss and commitment loss trajectories should stay close to baseline; (5) the judgement: Stage3 test_recall@10 of the single trained candidate versus the 0.0555 baseline and the 0.0638 previous best.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: BEHAVIOUR_OFF=true sets every D_i = 1, hence raw_k = 1, demand_k = 1, log1p demand is constant, off_k = 0 for all k, and level 1 is the pure curved assignment argmin_k d_c(u_i, q_k); levels 2-3, loss and STE unchanged. Code path exists and is unit-tested for exact zero offsets; no such arm is trained this round.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: GEOMETRY_OFF=true sets c = 0, so exp_0^0 = identity, d_c(x,y) = 2||x - y|| and S_ik = softmax_k(-2||v_i - a_k||/tau); level 1 becomes argmin_k(2||v_i - a_k|| - off_k), which reduces to the baseline Euclidean assignment when off is also zero. Code path exists and is unit-tested against the baseline quantiser to bitwise-level agreement on a random batch; no such arm is trained this round.
ABLATION BOTH ON: the single trained candidate: c = 1 curved level-1 distance plus the detached demand offset off_k, with levels 2-3, reconstruction, commitment and STE identical to baseline, trained once for 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four cards and evaluated by the frozen Stage3 protocol.

s    = sqrt(mean_i ||r1_i||^2)            (running mean, first 50 steps, buffer)
c    = 1 ; R_c = 1/sqrt(c) ; beta = cfg.commitment_weight (default 0.25)
tau  = clamp(mean over first 50 steps of mean_i min_k d_c(u_i,q_k), 0.01, 10)
D_i  = count_next(i in train split) / mean_j count_next(j)      # frozen, no grad
demand_k = 1 for all k                                          # buffer, no grad
# every step, level 1
v = r1 / s
u = exp0c(v)                       # tanh(sqrt(c)||v||) v / (sqrt(c)||v||), 0 -> 0
q = exp0c(a1)                      # a1 = baseline level-1 codebook parameter
Dk = (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh( clamp( sqrt(c) * || moebius_neg(u) (+) q ||, 0, 1-1e-6 ) )
S  = softmax_k(-Dk / tau)          # detached
raw_k = (S * D[None,:]).sum(0) / S.sum(0).clamp_min(1e-8)
demand = (1-rho)*demand + rho * raw_k * K1 / raw_k.sum().clamp_min(1e-8)   # rho = 1/48, no_grad
ell  = log1p(demand.clamp_min(1e-8))
off  = beta * (ell - ell.mean()).clamp(-ln3, +ln3)                          # detached
k1   = argmin_k (Dk - off)                                                  # ties -> smallest k
r2   = r1 - a1[k1]                                                          # same as baseline
# loss = baseline reconstruction + baseline commitment, STE unchanged
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: the level-1 residual batch r1 (B x 64), the baseline level-1 codebook a1 (K1 x 64), the frozen buffers s, c, tau, D (24,556), demand (K1), and the two boolean switches. Outputs: the hard level-1 index k1 (B, long) used for r2 and for the SID token, the updated demand buffer (K1, no grad), and the logged diagnostics (offset vector, assignment share, changed-assignment fraction). No change to the tensors returned to levels 2-3 apart from k1.
SAFEGUARDS: (i) artanh argument clamped to [0, 1 - 1e-6] and the Moebius sum norm

recomputed in float32 to avoid > 1 from rounding; (ii) exp_0^c guarded at ||v|| = 0 and ||v|| clamped to a maximum of 12 standardised units, so tanh never sees inf; (iii) demand floored at 1e-8, mean-normalisation denominator clamped, EMA held at 1 for the first 50 steps, all under torch.no_grad and detached; (iv) off_k hard-clipped to +-beta*ln3 so the behavioural term can break near ties but cannot override a clear geometric margin; (v) deterministic ties to the smallest index so k1 is reproducible across cards; (vi) s, tau, c computed on one rank and broadcast, NaN/Inf checked before being written to the buffers; (vii) the geometry-off path is unit-tested to reproduce the baseline quantiser, the behaviour-off path to produce exactly zero offsets, and both are logged in the run config although no arm is trained; (viii) D_i built only from the training split with an assertion that no validation/test sequence id is read.
END IDEA
